text: {"score":3,"justification":"The numbers match the card and the leaning is cautious and appropriate, but the narrative has an overstated headline, a wrong citation, and some unsupported speculation. An investigator would have to redo part of the analysis.","problems":["Headline says 99215 runs about three times expectation 'in every complexity band'. The card gives no per-band expected values; the by-complexity table shows ratios to the all-provider share of about 1.4 to 3.0, and band 0 is 2.6% vs 1.9%, only 1.4x. The 'two to three times in every band' claim is overstated.","Cites C0251638 (J06.9, 0 conditions) as an example of a single routine diagnosis but describes it alongside I10 and E11.9 claims; C0251371 is E11.9 (fine). Examples loosely fit, but the summary also calls C0251876/C0251878 '0-condition and repeat-patient' when they have 1 condition (CKD), which is a misstatement.","The 'soft signal' about templated or cloned notes is speculative. C0251432 is a one-condition visit documented at high MDM, but missing time is not evidence of cloning, and the card shows 1 of 4 supported examples with time recorded, so the point is weak.","The rationale repeats itself: the 0% below-billed finding appears twice, and the low-complexity share of 21% is described as '0 or 1 conditions' while the card field is 'low_complexity_share_of_99215', which is not defined precisely.","The next steps are generic: they ask for a larger sample of 99214 and 99215 claims and a re-screen, and do not name the specific low-complexity claims that the rationale says to request. The rationale and next_steps are inconsistent.","The 14 notes with moderate-plus data reviewed and only 1 lacking a lab line is mentioned without interpretation, and the summary does not flag that most documented claims were 99214 and not 99215."]}
